parameters.jsCode:
const g = $('Approval Gate').first().json;
const body = g.delivery_mode === 'EMAIL_BODY'
  ? g.content
  : (g.cover_note || 'Please find the document attached.');
const artefact = {
  EMAIL_BODY: 'no file. The draft text would be the email body.',
  PDF_ATTACHMENT: 'a Google Doc "' + g.document_name + '" in the matter folder, exported to PDF and attached.',
  DOCX_ATTACHMENT: 'a Google Doc "' + g.document_name + '" in the matter folder, exported to DOCX and attached.',
  DRIVE_LINK: 'a Google Doc "' + g.document_name + '" in the matter folder, shared with '
    + g.recipient + ' as reader, and the link put in the email body.',
}[g.delivery_mode];

const lines = [
  'DRY RUN. Nothing was sent and nothing was shared.',
  '',
  'Every approval check passed. This is what would have happened:',
  '',
  'Matter: ' + g.matter_id + '  ' + g.matter_title,
  'Action: ' + g.action_id,
  'Draft: ' + g.draft_id + '  (hash ' + g.content_hash + ')',
  'Approval: ' + g.approval_id,
  'Delivery: ' + g.delivery_mode,
  'Would create: ' + artefact,
  'Gmail To: ' + g.recipient,
  'Gmail Subject: ' + g.subject,
  '',
  '--- EMAIL BODY THAT WOULD BE SENT ---',
  body.slice(0, 1800),
  '--- END ---',
  '',
  'State was not changed. The approval is still PENDING and the action is still AWAITING_APPROVAL.',
  'Set dry_run to false in the Config node of workflow 4, then approve again to send for real.',
];
return [{ json: { reply: lines.join('\n').slice(0, 3900),
  intended: JSON.stringify({ matter_id: g.matter_id, action_id: g.action_id, draft_id: g.draft_id,
    approval_id: g.approval_id, delivery_mode: g.delivery_mode, recipient: g.recipient,
    subject: g.subject, content_hash: g.content_hash }) } }];

parameters.content:
## 4 - Research, Drafting, Approval and Dispatch

`route_group = DRAFT` builds the next draft version. `route_group = APPROVAL` runs the gate.

### The gate is pure code
**Approval Gate** decides, not Claude. It refuses unless all of these hold: the decision came from the owner chat, the approval exists and is still PENDING, the draft `content_hash` still equals the hash recorded when the approval was raised, that draft is the newest version for the action, the channel is GMAIL, the recipient is a valid address, no `[MISSING:]` placeholder survives, and no OUTBOUND communication already exists for the action.

### DRY_RUN
`Config.dry_run` is a string, `true` or `false`. When it is `true` and every check has passed, the gate returns DRY_RUN instead of SEND. No Gmail call is made, no Drive file is created, no Drive file is shared, and no approval or action state changes. The intended action is written to the Communications tab as `OUTBOUND_DRY_RUN` and reported to Telegram. That direction value is not `OUTBOUND`, so a dry run never blocks the later real send.

### Delivery
Approving approves two things at once, and the Telegram message names both. `Approve + send` uses the mode recorded on the approval row: a PDF attachment for employment and contractor documents, the email body otherwise. `Approve + share link` creates a Google Doc in the matter folder, shares it with the recipient as reader with no Google notification, and emails the link.

nodes.name: Reselect Action If Drafted
nodes.notes: B5: corrects Build Draft Context's action pick so an already-drafted action is not chosen forever.

nodes.name: Log Send Intent

value.subject: ={{ $('Approval Gate').first().json.subject }}
value.summary: Send attempted but not yet confirmed. If this row is still PENDING, the outcome of the send is unknown.

nodes.notes: D6: writes OUTBOUND_PENDING before any send, so an unconfirmed attempt is visible to the duplicate check.

nodes.name: Mark Send Failed
nodes.notes: D6: flips the PENDING row to OUTBOUND_FAILED so a genuinely failed attempt stops blocking a retry.

nodes.name: Preview Complete?
nodes.notes: A6. True only when the owner is looking at the whole draft. False on truncation and on assembly fault, which routes to the reject/edit-only keyboard.

nodes.name: Telegram - Approval Request (Review First)
nodes.notes: A6. Same text, but no Approve buttons. Used when the preview is an extract or the assembly faulted. The typed APPROVE command is still in the text, so the owner keeps a route to approval after reading the complete draft on the Drafts tab.

nodes.name: Integrity Guard
nodes.notes: Fail-closed containment. Refuses the branch whenever more than one Action row could be selected, so the first/last selection mismatches downstream become unreachable. Chooses nothing, ranks nothing, writes nothing.

nodes.name: Integrity OK?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean. False routes to Halt, which performs no I/O of any kind.

nodes.name: Verify Selected Row
nodes.notes: Second fail-closed gate, immediately before Gate Result and therefore before every state writer and every Gmail node. Re-derives the row and compares the fingerprint carried by Integrity Guard.

nodes.name: Selected Row Verified?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean. False routes to Halt, before Gate Result and therefore before every writer.

nodes.name: Halt - Data Integrity Conflict
nodes.notes: Terminal. Performs no I/O: no sheet write, no Telegram, no Gmail, no Drive. The conflict detail is visible in the execution record. Deliberately silent rather than notifying, because adding a send here would add an external dispatch path to a containment guard. Owner notification is a separate decision.

nodes.name: Load Conflict Notices
nodes.notes: Read-only. onError is continueErrorOutput so an unreachable or missing register routes to Halt rather than returning an empty list, which the resolver would otherwise read as a first occurrence. The ConflictNotices tab does not exist yet: this branch is unreachable until a conflict occurs, and the draft is unpublished.

nodes.name: Resolve Conflict Notice
nodes.notes: Read-before-write. Computes the deterministic conflict_key, decides FIRST or REPEAT, and fails closed if the register already holds more than one row for the key. Writes nothing. Carries no recipient, channel, description or draft content.

nodes.name: Notice Writable?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean on notice_action. Only FIRST or REPEAT may write. FAIL_CLOSED routes straight to Halt.

nodes.name: Upsert Conflict Notice
nodes.notes: The only writer to ConflictNotices. Writes exactly the 12 schema columns: no recipient, no channel, no description, no draft content. Upsert on conflict_key is NOT relied on for uniqueness; the read before it and the verify after it are what enforce that.

nodes.name: Reload Conflict Notices
nodes.notes: Fresh read after the write, so the verifier sees what is actually stored rather than what was intended.

nodes.name: Verify Conflict Notice
nodes.notes: Post-write verification. Google Sheets has no unique constraint and appendOrUpdate is not atomic against a concurrent writer, so this cannot prevent a race. It detects one and revokes notify eligibility. It never repairs.

nodes.name: Evaluate Send Eligibility
nodes.notes: Four conditions, all required. Destination is the fixed owner chat from Config and is never read from an Action row. Payload carries identifiers only: no recipient, channel, description or draft content. Sends nothing.

nodes.name: Send Eligible?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean. False routes straight to Classify, which records no change.

nodes.name: Send Conflict Notice (PLACEHOLDER - NO SENDER BUILT)
nodes.notes: DELIBERATELY INERT. This is where a real fixed-owner Telegram node would go. It performs no I/O and returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED, which Classify maps to no status change and no attempt burned. Publishing WF4 therefore cannot send anything: notices accumulate as PENDING and stay visible in the daily digest. Replacing this with a real sender requires its own approval.

nodes.name: Classify Notification Outcome
nodes.notes: The only node permitted to set SENT, FAILED, EXHAUSTED or notified_at. SUCCESS is the only outcome that yields SENT; every other outcome leaves the notice notifiable or escalates it. Diagnostics are redacted.

nodes.name: Status Write Needed?
nodes.notes: Only a real SUCCESS or a real failure changes the register. NOT_IMPLEMENTED and NOT_ELIGIBLE route straight to Halt.

nodes.name: Record Notification Result
nodes.notes: Writes only the four notification fields plus last_seen_at. Never touches action ids, fingerprints or any other register.

nodes.name: Reload After Notification
nodes.notes: Fresh read so the verifier sees what is stored, not what was intended.

nodes.name: Verify Notification Record
nodes.notes: Detects the sent-but-not-recorded case, where a message left and the status write did not land. It cannot prevent the resulting duplicate on the next run; it names it and escalates. No exactly-once guarantee is claimed anywhere.

nodes.name: Build Integrity Halt Notice
nodes.notes: No I/O. Normalises every item shape that can reach the containment terminus into one reporting shape. Carries identifiers, codes and row metadata only: never draft content, recipient, subject, facts or model output. Escapes for HTML before measuring length.

nodes.name: Log Integrity Halt
nodes.notes: One audit row per integrity halt. appendOrUpdate on a deterministic event_id, so a repeated identical conflict updates one row. continueRegularOutput and alwaysOutputData so a Sheets failure cannot suppress the owner notice downstream.

nodes.name: Telegram - Integrity Halt
nodes.notes: Owner notice for a fail-closed stop. Destination is Config.owner_chat_id only, never a register row, so this is not a dispatch path. Text is pre-escaped in Build Integrity Halt Notice. No approval command is offered.

nodes.name: Integrity Halt Reported
nodes.notes: Terminal. The containment path now ends here, after the owner has been told and the audit row written.

nodes.name: Unknown Route - Fail Closed
nodes.notes: No I/O. Mode's fallback previously drafted on an unrecognised route_group. This converts it into the guard's halt shape so it reaches the containment terminus instead.

nodes.name: Build Notification Failure Record
nodes.notes: Runs only on the error output of Telegram - Integrity Halt. No I/O. Mints its own event id under a different prefix so it can never overwrite the halt row. Does not resend and does not retry.

nodes.name: Log Notification Failure
nodes.notes: Second Events row: the integrity halt could not be delivered. Matched on its own event_id, so the original DATA_INTEGRITY_HALT row is never touched. Retries the SHEET WRITE only; it never retries the Telegram send.

nodes.name: Integrity Notice Undelivered
nodes.notes: Terminal. Distinct from Integrity Halt Reported on purpose: reaching THIS node means the halt happened and the owner was NOT told. The matter stays blocked either way.
